h1: The 6 Best Built-In Microwaves of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six built-in microwaves and drawer models, compared on size, wattage, cooking sensors and installation needs for kitchens.
summary: The Sharp SMD2420MS is the best built-in microwave, a 24 inch under-counter drawer with 1.2 cu ft, touch controls and sensor cooking. The thermomate offers finer power control, KoolMore adds memory presets, and the COSMO suits a 30 inch opening. The Frigidaire Gallery brings the largest capacity but needs a separate trim kit.
intro: Two very different appliances share the label built-in. One is a door microwave that sits in a wall opening and needs a trim kit to look finished. The other is a drawer that slides in beneath a counter and opens like a dishwasher drawer. Order the wrong shape and the cutout simply will not work.

Eight microwaves were reviewed and six kept, all designed for built-in installation. Two countertop models were left out because they are not built-in units. Ranking leaned on listed capacity, wattage, sensor cooking, width and installation notes, so measure your opening before anything else.

products.name: Sharp SMD2420MS 24-Inch Built-In Microwave Drawer Oven
products.verdict: A 24 inch under-counter drawer with sensor cooking and touch controls.
products.description:
Sharp's SMD2420MS is a 24 inch microwave drawer oven that fits under a counter. It holds 1.2 cubic feet and offers a touch control panel and sensor cook technology. It sits in the $500+ tier.

A drawer puts the controls and food at a comfortable height, which suits an island or lower cabinet, and this listing documents the clearest feature set of the group. The thermomate matches the sensor cooking but carries a less familiar brand, and the other Sharp has a much thinner listing.

Buy it for a kitchen island or a lower cabinet where reaching up to a wall unit is awkward. The caveat is price and installation: it needs a cabinet cutout sized for a 24 inch drawer, and it costs a premium over a countertop model.
products.skipIf: You want a standard door microwave.

products.name: thermomate 24 Inch Built-in Microwave Drawer
products.verdict: 1000 watts with 11 power levels, touch controls and sensor cooking.
products.description:
The thermomate is a 24 inch built-in microwave drawer rated at 1000 watts, with 11 power levels, touch controls and sensor cooking. It sits in the $500+ tier.

It offers more power levels than any rival here, which lets you fine tune delicate jobs such as melting or gentle reheating. It ranks second because the Sharp SMD2420MS lists the same sensor technology with a stronger brand name, and brand matters for service and parts on a built-in appliance.

Choose it if you like precise control and do not mind a lesser-known maker. Skip it if you want a major brand behind the unit. As with any drawer, confirm the cabinet opening and ventilation notes in the manual before ordering.

products.name: KoolMore 24 Inch Stainless-Steel Microwave Drawer with 1.2 cu. ft.
products.verdict: 1000W with 10 cooking levels, memory and timer functions.
products.description:
KoolMore's KM-MD-1SS is a 24 inch stainless steel microwave drawer with 1.2 cubic feet of space, 1000W of power and 10 custom cooking levels. It remembers presets, has timer functions and mounts flat on the bottom of a cabinet. It sits in the $500+ tier.

Memory presets are the draw for repeat recipes, since you can store a favorite sequence and reuse it. It ranks third because it has one fewer power level than the thermomate and the listing mentions no sensor cooking, which is useful for reheating.

Pick it if you cook the same dishes often and want one-touch settings. Skip it if sensor cooking is important to you. The premium tier means it is a considered purchase, so check the stainless finish matches your other appliances.

products.name: Sharp SMD2470ASY 24 in. 1.2 cu. ft. Built-In Microwave Drawer Oven
products.verdict: A 24 inch, 1.2 cubic foot Sharp drawer oven.
products.description:
The Sharp SMD2470ASY is a 24 inch, 1.2 cubic foot built-in microwave drawer oven. It shares its size and brand with the leader, and sits in the $500+ tier.

What it lacks is documentation. The listing gives few features next to the SMD2420MS, so you cannot confirm controls, sensor cooking or power levels from the page. That uncertainty is what ranks it fourth, even though the Sharp name and drawer format are attractive.

Buy it if the SMD2420MS is unavailable and you want to stay with Sharp. Before ordering, read the full product page and manual for the controls and installation details. If features matter, the thermomate or KoolMore lists more.
products.idealFor: A Sharp drawer when the first is out.

products.name: COSMO 30 in. Haven Coll 1.2 cu. ft. Built-in Microwave Drawer
products.verdict: A 30 inch, 1.2 cubic foot drawer for wider cabinets.
products.description:
COSMO's Haven Collection microwave is a 30 inch, 1.2 cubic foot built-in drawer. It sits in the $500+ tier and is meant for wider cabinet openings.

Width is its one distinction. Where the other drawers fit a 24 inch opening, this suits a 30 inch space, which helps a kitchen with a wide lower cabinet. It ranks fifth because the listing gives no sensor or power-level detail, and it will not fit the opening most of the others need.

Choose it if your cabinet is 30 inches wide. Skip it if your opening is 24 inches, since it will not fit. The thin specs mean you should read the manual online to check wattage and controls first.

products.name: Frigidaire Gallery Series GMBS3068BF 2.2 cu. ft. Built-in Microwave
products.verdict: A 2.2 cubic foot built-in, with the trim kit sold separately.
products.description:
Frigidaire's Gallery GMBS3068BF is a 2.2 cubic foot built-in microwave. The trim kit is sold separately, and the listing shows little else about its features.

Capacity is the biggest here, which suits large casserole dishes in a wall cabinet. It comes last because the trim kit adds cost and without it you get gaps around the unit. The drawer models above document more features, and the 2.2 cu ft size is a poor match for a drawer-style opening.

Buy it for a wall opening and big dishes. Skip it if you want a finished look out of the box. Budget for the trim kit, and confirm the matching kit number on the product page.
products.idealFor: Large dishes in a wall cabinet.

whatMatters.detail: A drawer microwave opens like a cabinet drawer and sits low, while a door model sits in a wall opening at eye level. Drawers are easier on the reach but cost more, which matters for budget. Check the title for the word drawer, and look at where the unit will sit in your kitchen. Reach comfort is the real payoff.

Built-in units are made for 24 or 30 inch openings, and those dimensions are fixed, so a wrong order means a return or a remodel. Measure the cutout height, width and depth, then compare with the listing. The Sharp and thermomate are 24 inches wide, and the COSMO is 30. No forgiving tolerance exists here.

Some door models need a separate trim kit to look finished, otherwise gaps show around the unit and the install looks unfinished. The Frigidaire Gallery lists one as sold separately. Check the listing for trim kit notes, and add that cost to your budget before comparing prices between models. Always read the box contents list.

Wattage affects cooking speed, and 1000 to 1200W is typical, so a lower number means longer reheating. The thermomate and KoolMore both list 1000W. Find the figure in the specs, and note that several listings here, like the Sharp SMD2470ASY, do not state it at all. Missing figures deserve a question to the seller. Ask before you buy.

Sensor cooking adjusts time based on steam from the food, which helps with reheating and avoids overcooking leftovers. The Sharp SMD2420MS and thermomate list it, but the KoolMore does not. Look for sensor cook in the bullet points of each listing if you reheat meals often. Skip it if you only warm drinks. Verify it before checkout.

faq.a: It is a microwave designed to sit in a cabinet or wall opening instead of on the counter. Drawer types, like the Sharp SMD2420MS, slide in beneath a counter, while the Frigidaire Gallery is a door model sized at 2.2 cubic feet.

Ordering before measuring the cutout. Sizes are fixed at 24 or 30 inches, so compare the Sharp and thermomate at 24 inches, or the COSMO at 30, with your actual opening in height, width and depth before you click buy.

faq.q: Is a drawer worth it over a door model?
faq.a: For comfort, yes, because the controls and food sit at a convenient height and you avoid reaching over a hot dish. But drawers like the Sharp, thermomate and KoolMore all fall in the $500+ tier, so you pay noticeably more than for a door model.

faq.q: Do I need a trim kit?
faq.a: The Frigidaire Gallery lists a trim kit as sold separately, so budget for it. The drawer models, including the Sharp and KoolMore, are designed to fit their openings, but confirm trim requirements in each manual before ordering.

Follow the maker's cutout and ventilation notes, and consider a professional installer. Built-in units like the KoolMore mount flat on the bottom of a cabinet and need proper clearance around them, so double-check the spec sheet before cutting anything.

faq.q: Can I put a countertop microwave in the opening?
faq.a: Not safely. Built-in units such as the Sharp or Frigidaire are designed for the ventilation of a cabinet or wall opening, and a countertop model may overheat in that tight space. Buy a unit that is made to be enclosed.

finalTake: Measure the cutout first, then choose the style. The Sharp drawer is the strongest all-round buy for a 24 inch space, thermomate and KoolMore suit cooks who want more control, and the COSMO covers wider cabinets. Pick the Frigidaire only if a wall opening and big dishes matter more than a finished look out of the box.
